gallery.title: File:Centennial Board of Finance 1875.jpg

gallery.credit: Sammlung eines Mitglieds des Ersten Deutschen Historic-Actien-Clubs e.V. (EDHAC e.V.); (kl)
gallery.description: Stock certificate for five shares to finance the Centennial International Exhibition 1876, issued by the Centennial Board of Finance and dated August 18, 1875. The share text is framed by extensive views. They portray the agricultural, industrial, and political development of the US. In addition, people from all continents pay homage to Lady Liberty and present goods they export to the US.

gallery.filename: Beaver Falls Cutlery Works (940).jpg
gallery.title: File:Beaver Falls Cutlery Works (940).jpg
gallery.credit: Scan of microfilm from Beaver County Industrial Museum, Darlington, Pennsylvania.
gallery.description: Photograph of an outsized carving knife and fork made by Beaver Falls Cutlery Works, Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania. The knife measured 9 feet 7 inches long. The handles were each made from a whole elephant's tusk, and were carved. The steel knife blade and the fork guard were etched with portraits, pictures and designs. Chinese workers, who were contracted between 1872 and 1877 at the works, helped to make these. The present whereabouts of the knife and fork is unknown.

gallery.filename: A lantern slide of the 1831 Locomotive "John Bull" at the Centennial International Exhibition in Philadelphia in 1876 (4743941103).jpg
gallery.title: File:A lantern slide of the 1831 Locomotive "John Bull" at the Centennial International Exhibition in Philadelphia in 1876 (4743941103).jpg
gallery.artist: William Creswell from Bremerton, Washington, USA
gallery.description:
The oldest operating locomotive in the world as seen in 1876. Originally built in England in 1831, it was made for the Camden and Amboy Railroad in New Jersey.
It now resides in the Smithsonian Museum of American History in Washington D.C. and is still in operating condition.
Full story here:

en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bull_(locomotive)

gallery.filename: Catalogus van de Vereeniging ter bevordering van de belangen des boekhandels voor de wereldtentoonstelling in Philadelphia, 1876 - BBB-826.jpg
gallery.title: File:Catalogus van de Vereeniging ter bevordering van de belangen des boekhandels voor de wereldtentoonstelling in Philadelphia, 1876 - BBB-826.jpg
gallery.artist: Vereeniging ter bevordering van de belangen des boekhandels (uitgever/publisher)
gallery.description: Deze catalogus van in Nederland uitgegeven boeken die te zien waren op de wereldtentoonstelling in Philadelphia in 1876, telt 240 bladzijden en geeft met 2098 nummers (met prijsvermelding) een ruime en zeer gevarieerde indruk van onze boekproductie in die dagen. Niet alleen de prestigieuze uitgaven zijn getoond, maar ook 'gewone' boeken en zelfs plaatselijke kranten als het Veendammer Advertentieblad en de Nieuwe Boeren-Goudmijn.
